solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boy briefly caught in hail overhead

indicators.note: one piece is trapped within another, like something caught in a net

parts.note: AVE is a Latin greeting, 'hail!'

indicators.note: cut short, so the word boy loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lad is pelted by hailstones falling from the sky above.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overhead is located higher up, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A Yank raised total weight of aircraft

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word reads it from the bottom up, so it is reversed

parts.note: to yank is to pull sharply

explanation.surface: An American lifting up the combined load of a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is the verb meaning pull; 'raised' turns PULL into LLUP below A.
explanation.definitionFit: All-up weight is the aviation term for an aircraft's complete loaded weight in flight.

clue.text: Bolt case after adjusting bar

indicators.note: the letters of these words are set in a new order, as if tinkered with

explanation.surface: Securing a box with a bolt once a rod has been fitted properly.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar is a barrier or impediment, a synonym for something in the way.

clue.text: Judge meets up with European

indicators.note: joins the two pieces side by side
in a down clue, reading upwards reverses the word meets

explanation.surface: A magistrate encounters someone from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' reads as a noun, a magistrate, but the definition is the verb: to judge or consider.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem is to judge or regard someone in a certain way, as in 'I esteem it an honour'.

clue.text: Quartz that's still pit-coal, oddly

indicators.note: take the letters in odd-numbered positions: first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A mineral found down a disused coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Quartz is the crystalline form of the compound silicon dioxide, an example of the class.

clue.text: Skirt I located after thirty seconds?

indicators.note: the letter I is placed following the other piece

parts.note: half a minute, so half the word MINUTE, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A skirt found within half a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: Thirty seconds is half a minute, so the clue takes half of MINUTE: MIN. MIN is also the usual abbreviation for minute.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini is a very short skirt, the miniskirt clipped.

clue.text: In New York, a road outside area of tavern

parts.note: RD is the address abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A street in Manhattan running past a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' looks like a containment signal, but it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn yard is the open courtyard of an inn, where coaches once drew up.

clue.text: Pi cousin's somehow causing scepticism!

indicators.note: by some unstated means, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative of the number pi is somehow arousing doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspicion is a feeling of mistrust, close in meaning to doubting scepticism.

clue.text: Ill at ease as gum provides savoury filling

indicators.note: unwell, out of sorts, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone uncomfortable chewing gum finds comfort in a savoury pie filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced, seasoned pork used to stuff pies, rolls and poultry is a classic savoury filling.

clue.text: Composer's last letter found in register

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: one piece is located within another

parts.note: a register is a list
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A composer's final letter discovered in an official record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last letter' looks like the end of a word in the clue, but it is Z, the alphabet's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Public service's lack of purpose when missing leader

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: without its opening letter, the head of the word is dropped

parts.note: futility is pointlessness, lack of purpose

explanation.surface: A public body is aimless when nobody is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link; 'missing leader' drops the F from FUTILITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A utility is a company providing gas, water or electricity, an essential public service.

clue.text: Cast top layer, staying inside

indicators.note: the letters are found within the run of words that follows across their breaks

explanation.surface: A plaster cast whose top layer stays put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' is not a plaster mould here but a play's company.
explanation.definitionFit: The cast of a play is its set of performers, the people who act.

clue.text: A friend, you are not getting paid

parts.note: a mate is a friend
UR is text-speak for 'you are'

explanation.surface: Telling a friend they are working for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur takes part for love rather than money, unpaid unlike a professional.

clue.text: Something stirring, etc, in tax reforms

indicators.note: reshapes, so these letters are formed again in another order

explanation.surface: Changes to taxation causing a stir, and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: An excitant is a stimulant, an agent that rouses or excites activity.

clue.text: Cat in bag: initially hard to put up with

indicators.note: the cat goes inside the bag

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch
a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: only the opening letter of hard is used

explanation.surface: Putting a cat in a bag is hard to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate or endure it, an idiom from digesting food.

clue.text: Tear wildly into the scene of operations

indicators.note: the jumbled piece goes inside the other word
in an unruly way, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone charging madly onto the battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating theatre is where surgery happens, and a theatre of war is a scene of military action.

clue.text: Asian state broadcast match lacking in colour

indicators.note: spoken over the airwaves, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a tie is a cup match; wan means pale

explanation.surface: An Asian country's game shown on monochrome television.
explanation.walkthrough: TIE WAN, said aloud, sounds like the island's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwan is a self-governing island in East Asia, an example of a state there.

clue.text: I go off course in SA mountain range

indicators.note: these letters go inside SA

parts.note: taken as written: SA is South Africa
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A hiker strays off the trail in South African mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged chain of peaks, from the Spanish word for saw.

clue.text: Posting message, initially poorly

indicators.note: only the opening letter of message is used

parts.note: poorly in British use means unwell, ailing

explanation.surface: Sending off a message that started badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' looks like an adverb but is the British adjective for sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Mailing is sending letters by post, the act of posting.

clue.text: Something snappy held up by protagonists!

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading upwards reverses the letters
the letters are held within the next word
together with 'held' it says the word protagonists holds them

parts.note: the letters ROTAG are hidden here

explanation.surface: A sharp remark delayed by the main characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held ... by' hides ROTAG in protagonists, and 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gator, short for alligator, has a reptile's powerful snapping jaws.

clue.text: Mechanical device in pit containing a chain

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other letters

parts.note: a pit is a mine
CH is the abbreviation for chain, an old unit of length

explanation.surface: Winding gear in a colliery that has a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine is an apparatus with moving parts that does work, a synonym for mechanical device.

clue.text: Fellow placing tea on piano

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: cha is a colloquial word for tea
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A man setting a cup of tea down on a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is informal British English for a man or bloke.

clue.text: Sunday dinner, perhaps right next to oven

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: Sunday lunch sitting right beside the cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sunday roast is the traditional British weekend meal of roasted meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is one example of a Sunday dinner, hence 'perhaps' for the definition by example.

clue.text: Letter to be burned: react badly

parts.note: to char is to scorch or burn on the surface

indicators.note: not done properly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A letter must be burnt, and someone responds poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests correspondence, which fits the burning, but here it means a written symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is a written symbol such as a letter of an alphabet.

clue.text: Thespian to go off — about to return

indicators.note: to come back, so the letters are taken in the opposite direction

parts.note: food that goes off will rot
CA is circa, about

explanation.surface: An actor storms offstage, only to come back.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is a stage performer, after Thespis, the legendary first Greek actor.
